params.name: opts
params.let: ['No solution: the lines are parallel and never meet', 'Infinitely many solutions: the two lines coincide']

stem: Find graphically the solution set of the equations $L_1 : {=a}x + y = {=c}$ and $L_2 : {=ma}x + {=m}y = {=n}$. Which statement is correct?
solution: Put $L_1$ in the form $y = {=c} - {=a}x$. Put $x = 0$, then $y = {=c}$, so $(0, {=c})$ is on $L_1$. Put $x = 1$, then $y = {=c - a}$, so $(1, {=c - a})$ is on $L_1$. Draw $L_1$.

Put $L_2$ in the form $y = {=ic} - {=a}x$ (divide by ${=m}$). Put $x = 0$, then $y = {=ic}$, so $(0, {=ic})$ is on $L_2$. Put $x = 1$, then $y = {=ic - a}$, so $(1, {=ic - a})$ is on $L_2$. Draw $L_2$.
Both lines have slope $-{=a}$, so they never cross at a single point.
The lines are drawn: they are the same line or different parallel lines, according to their points. Here $L_1$ passes through $(0, {=c})$ and $L_2$ passes through $(0, {=ic})$.

distractors.text: Exactly one solution: the lines meet at one point

proposed_misconceptions.label: Confuses parallel with coincident lines
proposed_misconceptions.description: Cannot tell from the graph whether two same-slope lines are different (no solution) or the same line (infinitely many).

proposed_misconceptions.label: Assumes two lines always meet in one point
proposed_misconceptions.description: Expects a single intersection point even when the lines have equal slopes.

notes: Second equation is m times the first, with the constant either m times c (coincide) or shifted (parallel). Twist: the second line looks different.
